snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.

For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},\qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), conditionally on the scores, if \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), then for every \(z>0\)
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}\frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2},
\]
and the conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most \(\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}+1\).

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses none of \(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For arbitrary slack lower and upper profile envelopes the two displayed bounds need not coincide, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.

defs.def:count-adaptive-bandwidth: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

defs.def:triangular-profile-union: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

snapshot.stmt: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

defs.def:circular-thinning-witnesses: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

assumptions.ass:isolated-thin-profile-upper: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).
assumptions.ass:global-boundary-entropy: For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

snapshot.stmt: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).

defs.def:fano-tent-family: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses none of \(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For arbitrary slack lower and upper profile envelopes the two displayed bounds need not coincide, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one.  To formulate an arbitrary-modulus result that distinguishes the two regimes, one must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile; under the frozen two-argument class, the requested package of conclusions cannot hold.

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.

assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the centered conditional sub-Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. defs.def:honest-band-handle: Condition on the observed scores and calibrate all nonempty side averages over the finite disk-pattern family by their Gaussian union-bound radius; add the Lipschitz bias \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) at a positive selected count and the trace envelope \(L\) at a zero count, then difference the two sides to form \(\mathcal C_n\). For any two full observed laws, transfer simultaneous coverage between them with \(\operatorname{TV}\) to obtain the two-law expected-half-width obstruction. This handle does not perform local multiplicity calibration and does not replace full-observed-law distinguishability by score-only distinguishability.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one.  To formulate an arbitrary-modulus result that distinguishes the two regimes, one must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile; under the frozen two-argument class, the requested package of conclusions cannot hold.

If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.

\]

\[

\]

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

defs.def:count-adaptive-bandwidth: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).
defs.def:empirical-counts: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).
defs.def:expected-sup-risk: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.
defs.def:mass-adaptive-estimator: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

assumptions.ass:declared-modulus-lower-mass: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).
assumptions.ass:global-boundary-entropy: For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).
assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).
assumptions.ass:lipschitz-side-means: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:declared-profile-lower: \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the exact conditional Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).
assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.

assumptions.ass:global-boundary-entropy: For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).
assumptions.ass:lipschitz-side-means: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).
assumptions.ass:polynomial-lower-mass: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\kappa>2\), there are constants \(0<c_\kappa<C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(c_\kappa h^{\kappa}\le\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))\le C_\kappa h^{\kappa}\) for all sufficiently small \(h\). In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).

Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

defs.def:circular-thinning-witnesses: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

assumptions.ass:isolated-thin-profile-upper: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).
assumptions.ass:lipschitz-side-means: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:polynomial-lower-mass: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

snapshot.stmt: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).

defs.def:fano-tent-family: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.

snapshot.stmt: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.

defs.def:triangular-profile-union: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one.  To formulate an arbitrary-modulus result that distinguishes the two regimes, one must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile; under the frozen two-argument class, the requested package of conclusions cannot hold.

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define

B_{t,n}(x)=
\begin{cases}
L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
L,&N=0.
\end{cases}
\]

\[
\mathcal C_n(x)=\left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
\widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
satisfies, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\),
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]

Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge
\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
\left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]

For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},\qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), conditionally on the scores, if \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), then for every \(z>0\)
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}\frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2},
\]
and the conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most \(\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}+1\).

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the exact conditional Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.

assumptions.ass:lipschitz-side-means: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:polynomial-lower-mass: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:global-boundary-entropy: For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).
assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

snapshot.stmt: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

defs.def:circular-thinning-witnesses: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

snapshot.stmt: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).

defs.def:fano-tent-family: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). defs.def:count-adaptive-bandwidth: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one.  To formulate an arbitrary-modulus result that distinguishes the two regimes, one must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile; under the frozen two-argument class, the requested package of conclusions cannot hold.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the exact conditional Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

defs.def:honest-band-handle: Condition on the observed scores and calibrate all nonempty side averages over the finite disk-pattern family by the conditional tail radius supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), whose moment-generating-function bound is derived from the exact conditional Gaussian assumption; add the Lipschitz bias \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) at a positive selected count and the trace envelope \(L\) at a zero count, then difference the two sides to form \(\mathcal C_n\). For any two full observed laws, transfer simultaneous coverage between them with \(\operatorname{TV}\) to obtain the two-law expected-half-width obstruction. This handle does not perform local multiplicity calibration and does not replace full-observed-law distinguishability by score-only distinguishability.

Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[

 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[

 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]

\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one. Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[

 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(\gamma\) is also smaller than one quarter of the universal numerical risk constant furnished by \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
If \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the same lower bound.  Thus the displayed band attains the matched global expected-sup half-width frontier on the pervasive class and, when that subclass is nonempty, on the base class.

Independently of the preceding small-\(\gamma\) restriction, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
The sharper pointwise ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\), its matching ratio lower bound, and an exact score-law necessary-and-sufficient criterion are not asserted: the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can remain bounded at an isolated thin site, and score-law total variation alone does not control the distance between full observed laws.

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
The fallback event obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\},
\]
and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.  Consequently, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})

\[

\[

 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the centered score-conditional sub-Gaussian kernel condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\); there exist a regular conditional law \(K_{t,P}(z,du)\) of \(\varepsilon_t\) given \(X=z\) and a \(P_X\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\) such that, for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}|u|K_{t,P}(z,du)<\infty\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}uK_{t,P}(z,du)=0\), and \(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{\lambda u}K_{t,P}(z,du)\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), where \(\sigma>0\) is fixed and known.
assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\); there exist a regular conditional law \(K_{t,P}(z,du)\) of \(\varepsilon_t\) given \(X=z\) and a \(P_X\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\) such that, for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}|u|K_{t,P}(z,du)<\infty\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}uK_{t,P}(z,du)=0\), and \(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{\lambda u}K_{t,P}(z,du)\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), where \(\sigma>0\) is fixed and known.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

defs.def:count-adaptive-bandwidth: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).
defs.def:empirical-counts: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).
defs.def:expected-sup-risk: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.
defs.def:mass-adaptive-estimator: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

assumptions.ass:global-boundary-entropy: For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

assumptions.ass:lipschitz-side-means: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).
assumptions.ass:gaussian-errors: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\); there exist a regular conditional law \(K_{t,P}(z,du)\) of \(\varepsilon_t\) given \(X=z\) and a \(P_X\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\) such that, for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}|u|K_{t,P}(z,du)<\infty\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}uK_{t,P}(z,du)=0\), and \(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{\lambda u}K_{t,P}(z,du)\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), where \(\sigma>0\) is fixed and known.
assumptions.ass:declared-profile-lower: \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed inclusion and matched rate expose an internal limitation of the frozen arbitrary-modulus OEQ's lower-profile-only exact-characterization demand for the two-argument class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\): matching same-class bounds cannot recover the isolated polynomial frontier when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) declares one thin site, because the class still retains the pervasive subclass. This is a limitation of that class parameterization, not a refutation of any published estimator or workflow. An arbitrary-modulus formulation that separates isolated from pervasive thinning must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), fix an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\), and suppose \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\). For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), and every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
\]
there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the first conclusion, and it obeys the second conclusion whenever widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. These conclusions hold for every such assignment geometry; the circular laws are needed only as explicit nonemptiness witnesses.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\). For any admissible assignment geometry under the preceding premises, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), for every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n
\]
obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the global lower bound because \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\), and it obeys the ratio conclusion when widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. The circular witnesses in \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) certify explicit nonemptiness only. Thus, whenever the pervasive class is nonempty, the displayed band attains the matched global expected-sup half-width frontier on the pervasive and base classes.

Independently of the preceding pervasive-class conclusions, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Uniform local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union, the corresponding local-ratio converse for unions without a nonempty pervasive component, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient criterion stated only through score-law total variation remain open. defs.def:count-adaptive-bandwidth: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

defs.def:fano-tent-family: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.
